kind: historical native diagnostic, before magnitude-scaled reciprocal and operation bounds
cause: A 64-epsilon absolute allowance on a reciprocal near 1e-26 was multiplied by a large squared width; the same absolute floor could straddle zero in a small positive squared Hessian denominator.
resolution: Magnitude-scaled operation and reciprocal allowances with gradual-underflow protection; separate binary-carry sum margins; homogeneous conversion back to physical units.
reproducer: diagnostic.cpp and diagnostic.py; the old primitive was pad(l,h) with error = 64*epsilon*(1+max(abs(l),abs(h))), also used inside reciprocal construction. The final sources use corrected arithmetic and do not reproduce the historical numbers byte for byte.
